items.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think more than – even in addition to all those great mentors, which I cherish, all, everywhere, from Clark – I talk to him all the time – Benny Carter.

ctx.x: That’s right. The trumpet players were way in the back. So I said, I’ll wait a little while now and get back to the trumpet section, but in marching band, I want to be up there with the – we used to beat the jocks. Every night, we’d waste them. They be in there showering and shaving and all that stuff. We gone. Then finally I got the trumpet. I always felt like it was about 15 years before I hit Hamp’s band [Lionel Hampton]. I had to go back. There’s a book coming out next month. Oh, my God. It just blew my head…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Well, I guess notably, Quincy Jones; that's the first one the pops into my mind.

ctx.x: Who are some of those people who have come since your time ... since your first ...

Well, I guess notably, Quincy Jones; that's the first one the pops into my mind. First name. Gee, Quincy ... I don't know when he came; he did "The Pawnbroker" -- I don't know what year that was. But up to now, he's done over 30 films, you know.
